## Today

- Why republics and democracies arose
- What they replaced
- How representative government works the idea
- Republic, democracy, and minority rights — including property

# Why This Matters

## Why This Matters

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
By the end of today you will explain why republics and democracies arose against abusive executives, define both terms, and show how representative government plus minority rights — including property — are two sides of the same project.
:::

# Why

## The problem was the executive

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 48px;"}
Kings turned tyrant — wealthy stationary bandits plundering those beneath them
:::

## Stationary bandit

![Roving versus stationary bandit incentive to protect production](../../assets/bandits.png){fig-alt="Diagram contrasting roving raiders with a stationary ruler who has incentive to protect production in order to tax it" width="90%"}

## Not a war on earned wealth

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 48px;"}
Property rights protection *for* earned wealth — against predation from above
:::

## Bargain and protection

![Lord and builders bargaining under a castle](../../assets/bandit_contract.png){fig-alt="Historical-style scene of a lord meeting builders, suggesting a bargain of protection for production" width="85%"}

## Pledge to protect

![Lord pledging to protect a village](../../assets/social_contract2.png){fig-alt="Scene of a lord pledging protection to a village community" width="85%"}

## Locke

![Portrait of John Locke](../../assets/locke.jpg){fig-alt="Portrait of John Locke" width="55%"}

## Legitimate government and property

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
Government exists to secure life, liberty, and property — not to be the chief predator
:::

# What

## Overthrow and evolution

- Rome: overthrow of kings
- Britain / Europe: evolution of parliaments and councils

## Top down, then broader

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
First upper classes constrain the king — later towns, then commoners gain representation and rights
:::

## Parliament evolution

![Vertical timeline of parliamentary expansion from barons to universal adult suffrage](../../assets/parliament_evolution.jfif){fig-alt="Vertical educational timeline of parliament evolving from great barons toward universal adult suffrage" width="42%"}

## Note on the timeline

Evolution of Parliament: **1215** great barons only → **1928** full women's suffrage in Britain.

# How

## Elected representative government

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 48px;"}
Congress and legislatures as the institutional answer to unconstrained executives
:::

## A democratic social contract

![Group meeting to form a democratic social contract](../../assets/social_contract.png){fig-alt="Scene of a mixed group meeting to form a democratic social contract without clear hierarchical social distinctions" width="85%"}

# Definitions

## Res publica and demos

![Side-by-side res publica and demos-kratos with shared civic assembly background](../../assets/respublikademoskratos.jfif){fig-alt="Side-by-side diagram of res publica and demos plus kratos over a shared assembly of citizens" width="92%"}

## Democracy

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 50px;"}
Rule by the people
:::

## Republic

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 50px;"}
*Res publica* — the public thing; government as the people's common affair
:::

## Historical accident

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
"Republic means not a monarchy" is largely a historical accident of labeling
:::

Both democracy and republic, in the Western story, were reactions to abusive executives.

# Aristotle

## True vs despotic forms

![Aristotle true versus despotic forms of government](../../assets/gemini_aristotle_2.jfif){fig-alt="Diagram of Aristotle true versus despotic forms of government including monarchy tyranny aristocracy oligarchy polity democracy" width="90%"}

## Warning in the vocabulary

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
For Aristotle, "democracy" could mean rule by the many for themselves — a corrupt form
:::

# Madison

## Pure democracy vs republic

![Madison contrast of pure democracy and republic](../../assets/madison_democracy.jfif){fig-alt="Two-column diagram contrasting pure democracy with a republic along Madison Federalist 10 lines" width="92%"}

## Federalist 10 in one line

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
Representation and a larger sphere filter faction; pure democracy amplifies it
:::

## Today's language

- Madison's "democracy" ≈ direct assembly / mob risk
- He did **not** oppose election of representatives
- Today's "liberal democracy" is much closer to what he called a republic

# Two sides of the same coin

## When the original point holds

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
Republic and democracy converge when minority rights — including property — are protected
:::

## That was the point

Against the stationary bandit and against majority plunder alike.

# Suffrage expansion

## U.S. path

![Schematic U.S. suffrage expansion timeline](../../assets/suffrage_evolution.jfif){fig-alt="Schematic timeline of U.S. suffrage expansion from a narrow founding electorate toward universal adult suffrage" width="92%"}

## Comparison note

- Britain: Parliament from **1215** (great barons) to **1928** (full women's suffrage)
- United States: **1789** already much broader than "barons only" → **1920** full women's suffrage

Historically fast expansion of who counts in "the people."

# Property, investment, prosperity

## Secure rights → invest → real wealth

![Property rights to investment to broad prosperity of the people](../../assets/property_rights.jfif){fig-alt="Three-step flow from secure property rights to investment and production to real wealth of ordinary people" width="92%"}

## Investment is broad

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 46px;"}
Not only stocks and bonds — education is an investment
:::

## You are investing now

Deferring current income and spending for a better life later.

Protection of broad-based property rights and expansion of democracy support broad-based prosperity.

# Discussion

## Prompts

- Is the United States a democracy, a republic, or both — and what hinges on minority (including property) rights?
- Why did constraining the executive come before full popular suffrage in the European story?
- How is your education an "investment" in the property-rights story?
